summary: SLA policy editor intermittently applies stale routing rules and macro templates; reporting export omits applied-rule metadata
description:
Issue summary: The internal SLA Policy Editor sometimes saves configurations that do not reflect in downstream routing decisions and macro/template application. Reporting exports (CSV via /admin/support-exports) are missing the applied_rule_id and template_version columns for affected changes.

Impact: Internal support workflows are misrouting tickets and applying outdated canned responses. Pager coverage and escalations were affected for ~45 tickets between 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-11. This is internal-only but blocks rapid incident triage and causes manual workaround overhead.

Environment: Production support-tooling stack (support-tooling service v2.8.1, sla-engine v1.3.4, routing-service v0.9.7) in us-east region. Changes were performed via Console (UI) and the /admin API.

Expected: When a user updates an SLA policy or routing rule and saves, the change should atomically update the rule store and be visible to the routing engine and reporting exports within the configured propagation window (<30s). Macro/template version used for a ticket should be captured in exports.

Actual: Intermittent stale rules observed: routing-service continues to act on previous rule set for 10–30 minutes. Exports generated during the window do not include applied_rule_id or template_version for tickets that should have been affected.

Initial hypothesis: Race between policy-store update propagation and caching layer in routing-service; reporting pipeline reads from cached view. Potential cached TTL misconfiguration or missing cache invalidation event when editor saves via API.

Attachments: log snippets, CSV export sample (attached to ticket), Console change event IDs.
steps_to_reproduce: Open SLA Policy Editor and change routing rule priority for 'p1-escalation' to route to 'oncall-escalation' (increment version)
Save change and record the Console change event id and timestamp
Attempt to recreate an incoming ticket (use support-test-hook) that matches the rule criteria
Observe routing behavior in routing-service logs and check exported CSV from /admin/support-exports during the 1-30 minute window after save
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11 09:12 UTC: Support tooling logs show policy-store write OK with event id evt_20260311_5134; event dispatched to pubsub topic 'policy-updates'.
2026-03-11 09:12:02 UTC: routing-service received pubsub message but processed event using cache snapshot stamped 2026-03-10T23:05:12Z (stale).
Cache layer TTL configured to 20m in routing-service (seen in config map). This is higher than intended 30s — likely root cause for delayed application.
Reporting export job (support-exports) reads from routing-service /state endpoint which currently serves cache view; export task did not subscribe to policy-updates topic.
comments: Priya Nair (Reporter) - 2026-03-11: Flagging after CS noticed repeated manual reroutes. Attached sample CSV and Console change event ids.

Diego Martinez (Assignee) - 2026-03-11: Investigating — initial logs suggest cache TTL misconfiguration. Spun up local repro against staging. Linking INT-7123 which touched routing invalidation behavior.

Liam O'Connor (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Confirmed routing-service config map had TTL override applied during a config rollout on 2026-02-28. Suggested hotfix to invalidate cache on policy-updates Pub/Sub messages.

Aisha Khan (Platform Eng) - 2026-03-13: Opened PR gh://redwood/sla-engine#1288 to emit explicit invalidation event. Also adding consumer in support-exports to subscribe to policy-updates (gh://redwood/support-tooling#1245).

Diego Martinez - 2026-03-14: Running canary for invalidation listener on routing-service in us-east; early results show routing applying new rules within ~8s for test events. Still validating export pipeline.
Product Ops (note) - 2026-03-14: Track impact metrics for tickets rerouted and manual overrides performed between 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-14.
resolution:
Workaround: Support agents were instructed to use manual 'force-refresh-rule' button in Console and to escalate via the 'oncall-escalation' alias until fix rolled out.

Fix implemented: Added explicit cache invalidation on policy-updates pubsub messages in routing-service (PR gh://redwood/sla-engine#1288) and added subscription in support-exports to read latest policy write events before building CSV (PR gh://redwood/support-tooling#1245). Decreased default cache TTL to 30s in routing-service config map and deployed canary to us-east on 2026-03-14.

Follow-ups: 1) Run a backfill task to reprocess exports for 2026-03-09..2026-03-11 window (task created INT-8460). 2) Add automated test for policy-update -> routing invalidation (E2E). 3) Add monitoring alert if routing-service applies policy older than 60s.

Status: Canary successful in us-east; plan to roll to other regions after 24h observation window.
